question: What is the capital of Kenya?
fact: Nairobi has a national park with lions and giraffes inside its city limits.

question: What is the capital of Brazil?
fact: Brasilia was built from scratch and became the capital in 1960.

question: What is the capital of Turkey?
fact: Istanbul is far bigger, but Ankara became the capital in 1923.

question: What is the capital of Argentina?
fact: Buenos Aires means 'good airs' or 'fair winds' in Spanish.

question: What is the capital of Thailand?
fact: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names on Earth.

question: What is the capital of New Zealand?
fact: Wellington is the southernmost capital city of any sovereign country.

question: What is the capital of Nigeria?
fact: Abuja officially replaced Lagos as Nigeria's capital in 1991.

question: What is the capital of Vietnam?
fact: Ho Chi Minh City was called Saigon until 1976.

question: What is the capital of Morocco?
fact: Casablanca is Morocco's largest city, but the government sits in Rabat.

question: Which city is the seat of the Swiss federal government?
fact: Swiss law calls Bern the 'federal city' rather than the capital.

question: What is the capital of Pakistan?
fact: Islamabad was purpose-built in the 1960s to replace Karachi.

question: What is the capital of South Korea?
fact: About half of all South Koreans live in the Seoul metropolitan area.

question: What is the capital of Peru?
fact: Lima is one of the driest capitals on Earth and rarely sees real rain.

question: What is the capital of Norway?
fact: Oslo was called Christiania for about 300 years.

question: What is the capital of Mongolia?
fact: Ulaanbaatar is often called the coldest national capital in the world.

question: What is the capital of Ethiopia?
fact: Addis Ababa hosts the headquarters of the African Union.

question: What is the capital of Chile?
fact: Chile's national congress meets in Valparaiso, not Santiago.

question: What is the longest river in South America?
fact: The Amazon carries about a fifth of all river water that reaches the oceans.

question: In which country is the temple complex of Angkor Wat?
fact: Angkor Wat appears on Cambodia's national flag.

question: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
fact: Russia stretches across 11 time zones.

question: Which is the smallest country in Africa by area?
fact: The Gambia is the smallest country on the African mainland.

question: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
fact: Counting its many islands, Canada's coastline is over 200,000 km long.

question: Lake Titicaca lies on the border of Peru and which other country?
fact: At about 3,800 m, it is one of the highest navigable lakes in the world.

question: Victoria Falls lies on the border of Zambia and which other country?
fact: Its local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means 'the smoke that thunders'.

question: Which mountain range is traditionally seen as a border between Europe and Asia?
fact: The Urals run about 2,500 km from the Arctic down towards Kazakhstan.

question: The Pyrenees mountains separate France from which country?
fact: The tiny country of Andorra sits high up in the Pyrenees.

question: What is the highest mountain in Africa?
fact: Kilimanjaro sits close to the equator yet has glaciers on top.

question: What is the highest mountain in South America?
fact: Aconcagua in Argentina is the highest peak outside Asia.

question: Which strait separates Europe from Africa?
fact: At its narrowest point it is only about 14 km wide.

question: The Bosphorus strait runs through which city?
fact: Istanbul is one of very few big cities that spans two continents.

question: What is the largest island in the world that is not a continent?
fact: Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.

question: Madagascar lies off which coast of Africa?
fact: Most of Madagascar's wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth.

question: Which country has three capital cities?
fact: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein each house one branch of government.

question: Which desert in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth?
fact: Some weather stations in the Atacama have never recorded rain.

question: Which country's flag shows a red maple leaf?
fact: Canada adopted the maple leaf flag in 1965.

question: Which country's flag is a plain red circle on a white background?
fact: Bangladesh's flag also has a red disc, but on a green background.

question: Which country's flag is made of two stacked triangles?
fact: Switzerland and Vatican City have square flags instead of rectangles.

question: Which river flows through Baghdad?
fact: Mesopotamia means 'land between rivers': the Tigris and the Euphrates.

question: The Danube flows into which sea?
fact: The Danube flows through ten countries, more than any other river.

question: Which river flows through Paris?
fact: Paris has 37 bridges across the Seine.

question: Which Italian city is built on more than 100 small islands linked by canals?
fact: Venice has no cars; boats and feet are the way to get around.

question: Iceland sits on top of which geological feature?
fact: In Iceland you can walk between the North American and Eurasian plates.

question: The volcanic 'Ring of Fire' surrounds which ocean?
fact: About three quarters of the world's active volcanoes lie along it.

question: Which line of latitude sits at 0 degrees?
fact: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs right through it.

question: The Prime Meridian passes through which capital city?
fact: France kept its own Paris-based time until 1911.

question: Counting its overseas territories, which country spans the most time zones?
fact: Thanks to islands across the globe, France spans 12 time zones.

question: How many official time zones does China use?
fact: In far western China the winter sun can rise near 10 am Beijing time.

question: Which very salty body of water lies between Israel and Jordan?
fact: Its shore is the lowest land on Earth, over 400 m below sea level.

question: What is the largest lake in the world by area?
fact: Despite its name, the Caspian Sea is usually classed as a lake.

question: What is the deepest lake in the world?
fact: Baikal holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.

question: What is the largest country in Africa by area?
fact: Algeria took the top spot when South Sudan split from Sudan in 2011.

question: What is the largest country in South America?
fact: Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.

question: Which two countries share the world's longest international border?
fact: The Canada-US border runs for about 8,900 km.

question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
fact: Lesotho is the only country lying entirely above 1,000 m.

question: Besides Paraguay, which South American country is landlocked?
fact: Bolivia still keeps a navy, which patrols Lake Titicaca.

question: In which city is the Taj Mahal?
fact: Emperor Shah Jahan built it as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

question: The ancient rock-carved city of Petra is in which country?
fact: Petra was carved by the Nabataeans more than 2,000 years ago.

question: Which city is home to the Sagrada Familia basilica?
fact: Work on Gaudi's basilica began back in 1882.

question: The Christ the Redeemer statue overlooks which city?
fact: The statue's outstretched arms span about 28 metres.

question: In which country is the giant sandstone rock Uluru?
fact: Uluru is sacred to the Anangu people, its traditional owners.

question: Which African country was once known as Abyssinia?
fact: Ethiopia has its own calendar, about seven to eight years behind ours.

question: Which island country was called Ceylon until 1972?
fact: Ceylon tea kept the old name and is still sold under it today.

question: Which country was known as Burma?
fact: Its largest city, Yangon, was the capital until 2006.

question: Which country was known internationally as Persia until 1935?
fact: Iranians had long called their own country Iran before the switch.

question: Which country has the most ancient pyramids?
fact: Sudan has around 200 Nubian pyramids, more than Egypt.

question: Which is the only country that covers an entire continent?
fact: From east to west, Australia is wider than the Moon.

question: Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in which country?
fact: Mount Fuji is an active volcano; it last erupted in 1707.

question: Which country has more lakes than any other?
fact: Canada is thought to hold more than half of all the world's lakes.

question: What is the longest mountain range on land?
fact: The Andes run about 7,000 km down the western side of South America.

question: Which country shares land borders with both France and Austria?
fact: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian, Romansh.

question: Which sea lies between Italy and the Balkan Peninsula?
fact: Venice, Split and Dubrovnik all sit on the Adriatic coast.
